cards.back: A sample where each member of the population has an equal chance of being selected. It is the best way to avoid bias.
A sample where members volunteer to participate. Often biased because those with strong opinions are more likely to respond.
A sample chosen by a rule, such as selecting every 10th person on a list. Can be easy to implement but may introduce bias if a pattern exists.
The population is divided into groups (strata) that share a characteristic, and a random sample is taken from each group. Ensures all subgroups are represented.
The population is divided into clusters, and entire clusters are randomly selected. All members of chosen clusters are included in the sample.
A sample that selects members of the population who are easy to reach. Usually biased because it does not represent the whole population.
An error that causes a sample to overrepresent or underrepresent part of the population. Biased samples lead to invalid conclusions.

cards.front: How can you create an unbiased random sample?
cards.back: Assign a unique number to each member of the population, then use a random number generator to select the sample. Every member has an equal chance.

cards.front: Why is a convenience sample often biased?
cards.back: It only includes people who are easily accessible, leaving out those who are harder to reach. This can produce results that do not reflect the entire population.

cards.front: What is an [[kw:experiment]] in data collection?
cards.back: A method where a treatment is imposed on individuals to measure its effect. Experiments can establish cause-and-effect relationships.
A method where individuals are observed and variables are measured without controlling the environment. It can show associations but not causation.
An investigation where every member of a sample is asked one or more questions. Surveys rely on self‑reported data.
A method that uses a model to reproduce the conditions of a real‑world process. Useful when actual experiments are impractical or dangerous.

cards.front: What is a [[kw:biased question]] in a survey?
cards.back: A question worded in a way that encourages a particular response or makes it hard to answer truthfully. It can lead to inaccurate survey results.
Split it into two separate questions that each address only one issue. This allows respondents to give accurate answers to each part.
